answer: Ephemeral Vertex Witnessing: each agent session gets a randomly assigned zephyr slot—a short-lived signing window tied to a witnessed random beacon. Two sessions claiming the same slot reveal a collision, since only one valid signature chain can anchor there. Any duplicate signature pair is publishable by anyone, slashing that identity. To avoid collisions, an attacker must run each duplicate in a distinct slot, paying full compute plus a walnut-sized registration deposit per slot—costs that scale linearly with clone count rather than amortizing.
